summary:
Lunala is an interactive navigator for exploring lunar south-pole landing sites and arrival dates. Users can inspect terrain in a 3D survey or polar map, move a timeline, simulate launch delays, and compare candidate regions by sunlight, direct-to-Earth visibility, terrain, and proximity to permanently shadowed areas. A Rust engine compiled to WebAssembly evaluates Sun and Earth positions against terrain horizons using NASA LOLA elevation data.

The project addresses the challenge of how a small change in location or arrival date can change the power and communication conditions a lunar mission faces. Lunala brings those factors into one accessible workspace to aid scientists and private corporations looking to build semi permanent to permanent sites on the moon.
details:
Lunala combines a guided lunar globe with a mission workspace. Users select a south-pole region, examine its 3D terrain or polar map, turn on layers such as elevation, slope, craters, sunlight, radio visibility, permanent shadow, and an ice favorability model, then move the UTC timeline or apply a launch delay. Explorer mode explains results in everyday language while planner mode exposes detailed priorities and controls. Users can rank promising areas, compare sites, and inspect the evidence behind the displayed layers.

An offline Python pipeline prepares NASA LOLA terrain, JPL Horizons Sun and Earth ephemerides, and other cited map products. A native Rust tool builds terrain-horizon data; the same Rust code is compiled to WebAssembly for browser-side evaluation and scoring. The interface uses TypeScript, React, Three.js with React Three Fiber, Tailwind CSS, and Vite. This approach makes changes to dates and priorities responsive while keeping the data sources and assumptions visible.

The creative part is the connection between a local terrain horizon and a changing mission window. The app shows why a ridge can offer useful sunlight while also limiting Earth contact, or why a launch delay can change a site’s ranking. We treated the long-term illumination maps separately from predictions for a selected arrival window. The ice layer represents modeled favorability, roughness is a terrain-derived rock proxy, and thermal estimates are simplified. Lunala supports the corporations and scientist looking to find and establish the best sites on the moon to complete their goals.
